original.statement: The storage version of the imagepolicies.image.toolkit.fluxcd.io CRD changes from v1beta2 to v1. Existing ImagePolicy objects stay stored as v1beta2 until rewritten, so they need a storage version migration and a status.storedVersions update before a later release removes v1beta2.

consequence.statement: After the upgrade, new and rewritten ImagePolicy objects are stored as v1. Existing objects stay stored as v1beta2, and the CRD's status.storedVersions still lists v1beta2. v1beta2 is still served in this release, so nothing fails. Before any future release that stops serving v1beta2, the stored objects would need migrating.
consequence.remediation: Optionally run a storage version migration: rewrite all ImagePolicy objects so they are stored as v1, then remove v1beta2 from status.storedVersions on the imagepolicies.image.toolkit.fluxcd.io CRD.

corrected.statement: The storage version of imagepolicies.image.toolkit.fluxcd.io changes from v1beta2 to v1. v1beta2 is still served, so existing ImagePolicy objects keep working but stay stored as v1beta2 until they are rewritten. This is a review item, not mandatory work, for this upgrade.

decision.reason: The validators, working from [ev-782bc47d120d] and [ev-c2c6c790d6b2], confirm that the storage version moves from v1beta2 to v1 and that v1beta2 is still an API version in both releases. So existing ImagePolicy objects stored as v1beta2 keep working after this upgrade, and nothing fails, is rejected or stops being honoured. The only evidence for a mandatory migration is the generic note in the computed diff about "a later release" removing v1beta2. No upstream evidence shown here says that removal is scheduled or deprecated. That makes migration-required (action) an over-claim, so the right kind is behavior-change (review), with the storage migration as recommended hygiene.
